Definition: Does the register cover births, deaths and marriages?
Comments: The Civil Registry Department's project documentation states the central database is kept updated with births, deaths, marriages and divorces (continuous registration), indicating full scope across these events.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, unchanged. The original UN pptx source could not be fetched (file format error). UNICEF's Sudan CRVS profile confirms legally-established registration processes (with electronic processing) for births (Child Act 2010/Civil Registry Act 2011), marriages (Muslim Personal Law Act 1991) and deaths; a 2012 review of the 2001 Civil Registration Act likewise confirms unified coverage of birth, death and marriage events. A 2025/26 ESCWA regional CRVS digitisation survey does not list Sudan among the countries still relying on paper for marital-status registration, consistent with digital coverage of all three event types. Value Code 3 (All) is corroborated by independent sources.

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: As a proxy for CRVS completeness, Landinfo cites Sudan MICS 2014 showing 67% of children under 5 were registered (birth registration), indicating mid-level completeness (50-69%).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, unchanged. UNICEF's own account of the 2014 MICS gives 67.3% national birth registration under age 5 (up from 59% in 2010), and a 2022 UNICEF Africa-wide birth registration brochure still cites this 2014 figure as the latest available — a UNICEF benchmarking report (Sept 2023) confirms no MICS has been conducted in Sudan since 2014. With no fresher nationally representative survey available (and civil war since 2023 precluding new data collection), 67% keeps the score at 50-69% (Value Code 3), now corroborated by two further UNICEF sources.

Definition: What proportion of the electorate does the register cover?
Comments: UN video report on the 2010 election process quotes Sudan's National Elections Commission saying voter registration reached 15,778,154 people, 81% of the targeted voting-age population, supporting 70-89% uptake for that period.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Downgraded from 70-89% to 50-69%. The cited 2009/2010 figure (81%, per NEC's own target-based measure) is superseded by the 2015 electoral roll, the last time the register was updated and used nationally. International IDEA data show 13,126,989 registered against a voting-age population of 19,667,400 (~67%) for the 2015 election, corroborated by the AU pre-election assessment mission (13.34 million eligible voters, with roughly 2.6 million Darfur IDPs excluded and parts of the roll carried over, unverified, from the pre-secession 2010 register). No national election or register update has occurred since (2019 revolution, 2021 coup, civil war from 2023), so ~67% is the most recent, best-supported figure, placing Sudan in the 50-69% band (Value Code 3).

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Officials cited to Landinfo reported 82% of the population registered (2016) and about 35.5 million of 40 million inhabitants registered in 2021 (~89%), with lower rates in peripheries/IDP areas; this supports 70-89% coverage category.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed but flagged for human review. Further searches (World Bank ID4D, UNICEF) did not surface an independent quantitative figure for population-register coverage; the 82% (2016) and ~89% (2021) figures still trace solely to unverified statements by Sudanese officials as reported in the Landinfo COI report. Other CRVS literature qualitatively corroborates high but geographically uneven coverage since the 2011 centralised registry, so the 70-89% band (Value Code 4) is retained, but the precise percentage should be treated cautiously given the lack of a second quantitative source and disruption from the civil war since 2023. Recommend human review to seek a corroborating quantitative source.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the business register?
Comments: Sudan Tax Authority project documentation lists the Commercial Registrar among prioritized entities identified for integration with the tax system, indicating planned/targeted integration (not necessarily implemented).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Planned to Partially integrated. The Tax Authority's own 2025 documentation states its cross-entity integration project — which explicitly includes the Commercial Registrar — is 'over 80%' implemented and ongoing, well beyond a merely planned stage. Its published tax procedures already impose a statutory obligation for the Commercial Registrar to notify the Tax Chamber monthly of company registrations, amendments and deregistrations, i.e. an operating (if not confirmed real-time/API) data-exchange mechanism. Independent corroboration from Sudanese press (October 2025) confirms a related entity (Customs) has completed a comparable digital integration with the Civil Registry via the 'Baladna' platform, indicating this wider interoperability programme is materially advancing rather than aspirational. Full/real-time technical integration specifically with the Commercial Registrar is not independently confirmed, so 'Fully integrated' is not warranted; some reliance on the Tax Authority's own reporting remains, so a light human check is advisable.
